BILL NUMBER:  S3715               REVISED 06/05/09

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the state technology law, in relation to renaming the
statewide wireless network advisory council as the statewide
interoperability executive committee


 PURPOSE :

This bill renames the "Statewide Wireless Network Advisory Council" as
the "Statewide Interoperability Executive Committee" and reorganizes
the composition of the Executive Committee.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill: (1) renames Article IV of the State Technology
Law (STL); (2) adds the head of the New York State Division of
Military and Naval Affairs (DNMA) and the director of New York's State
Emergency Management Office (SEMO) as ex officio members; (3) adds a
new power to permit the Executive committee to examine and recommend
State policy regarding interoperability of public safety
communications' systems; (4) designates the Chief Information Officer
(CIO) of New York State and the superintendent of the State police as
Co-Chairs; and (5) permits the co-chairs to appoint working groups
consisting of members of the Executive committee or their designees or
other representative of public or private entities to advise and
assist -the Executive Committee in carrying out its functions, powers
and duties.

Section 2 of the bill provides for the effective date.

 EXISTING LAW :
State Technology Law § 401 currently provides for a twenty-seven (27)
member Statewide Wireless Network Advisory Council, including: 14 ex
officio members representing State agencies and authorities, two
appointees of the Governor, five appointees each from the senate and
Assembly, and the state CIO, who serves as chair. One of the
Governor's appointments and three each of the appointments of the
Senate and the Assembly shall be a member, officer, or employee of a
first responder organization that serves a municipal corporation.
State Technology Law. § 402 provides the functions, powers and duties
of the Advisory Council.  State Technology Law § 403 requires local
governments to make annual reports of costs related to the statewide
wireless Network.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
This is a new bill.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :
The Statewide Wireless Network (SWN) project was undertaken to provide
a mobile radio and data communications network for use by public
safety and law enforcement. New York State, through the Office for
Technology, contracted with a technology vendor for a multi-phased
buildout. of the network across New York State. The Legislature
created the SWN Advisory Council in 2004 to assist with implementation
and to provide status reports to the Governor and Legislature. In the
first phase of build-out the vendor was unable to meet network
performance requirements and the State opted to end the contract. This
bill reconfigures the Advisory Council into an Executive Committee
that can continue to build upon already completed work and report on
alternative paths forward for a future interoperable statewide
communications system for first responders. An interoperable system
would ideally allow first responders from all jurisdictions and
agencies to communicate reliably during natural disasters or other
emergencies and ensure reliable and rapid sharing of information.  The
missions of DMNA and SEMO correspond in many ways with the powers and
duties of the Executive Committee. DMNA is a State agency that serves
as the headquarters for New York's militia forces (the Army National
Guard, the Air National Guard, the New York Guard and t.he New York
Naval Militia). Similarly, the mission of SEMO is to protect the lives
and property of the citizens of New York State from threats posed by
natural or manmade events. To fulfill this mission, SEMO coordinates
emergency management services with other federal and State agencies to
support county and local governments. The addition of these two new ex
officio members will enhance the expertise of the Executive Committee
as it moves forward with first responder interoperability
communications in New York State.  The Executive Committee will
benefit from allowing the co-chairs to appoint working groups such as
regional representative groups or technical issue groups to further
assist the Executive Committee in examining State policy on all
matters concerning interoperability or public safety communication
systems and emergency services.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :
None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This bill Shall take effect immediately.
